chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Any man from our Shias who goes to a man from his brethren to seek his assistance regarding his need, but he does not assist him while he is able, Allah will test him by making him fulfill the needs of others from our enemies, and Allah will punish him for it on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a Shia who refuses to help a brother in need?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the spiritual consequence of neglecting social solidarity within the Shia community. The Imam warns that refusing capable assistance to a brother results in a specific divine test: one’s efforts will be diverted to serving the needs of their enemies, serving as a precursor to punishment on the Day of Judgment. This underscores the concept of 'Ikhwa' (brotherhood) not merely as a label but as a binding ethical covenant with tangible metaphysical repercussions.
